rate.description: Zakat at 2.5% of the zakat base for a Hijri (lunar) year; for a Gregorian financial year the rate is prorated by days (365/354), giving 2.577683%.
rate.source_reference: Executive Regulations for Zakat Collection (Ministerial Resolution No. 1007 of 2024); ZATCA FAQ

base.description: Zakat base = added items (equity and equivalents, provisions treated as equity, non-current liabilities under Article 29, and the difference between adjusted and book net profit) less deducted items under Article 26 (investments, net fixed assets, intangibles, materials not for sale, statutory deposits, deferred tax assets). Subject to the Article 27 minimum and the Article 28 maximum.
base.verification_note: Structure read from ZATCA's English text of the Implementing Regulations for Zakat Collection 1445H (MR 1007 as amended by MR 1248), Articles 21 to 29. Article 25 proportional placement of current liabilities is not applied. Awaiting sign-off by the Oblique tax team against worked cases.
base.source_reference: Implementing Regulations for Zakat Collection 1445H (MR 1007 dated 19/08/1445H, amended by MR 1248 dated 11/10/1446H), Articles 21, 23, 24, 26, 29

mixed_ownership.description: Companies owned by both Saudi/GCC nationals and non-Saudi persons pay zakat on the Saudi/GCC share of the zakat base and income tax on the non-Saudi share of taxable profit.
mixed_ownership.source_reference: Income Tax Law (Royal Decree M/1 of 1425H), Art. 2; Zakat Regulations

min_base.description: Article 27: if the zakat base falls below adjusted net profit, the base becomes the lower of (a) undeducted assets plus the difference between adjusted and book net profit and (b) adjusted net profit. A negative base with no adjusted net profit gives no base; a positive base with no adjusted net profit stands.
min_base.verification_note: Read from the regulation text (Article 27 paragraphs 1 to 4). Awaiting technical sign-off.
min_base.source_reference: Implementing Regulations for Zakat Collection 1445H, Article 27

max_base.description: Article 28: the zakat base cannot exceed equity and equivalents per the year-end statement of financial position plus the difference between adjusted and book net profit (or loss). Equity includes items reclassified to equity: profits declared but undistributed (Article 36), partners' loans treated as equity (Article 30) and provisions treated as equity (Article 24).
max_base.verification_note: Read from the regulation text (Article 28 paragraphs 1 and 2). Awaiting technical sign-off.
max_base.source_reference: Implementing Regulations for Zakat Collection 1445H, Article 28

standard_rate.description: Corporate income tax at 20% of adjusted net profit attributable to non-Saudi/non-GCC shareholders. Oil and hydrocarbon producers taxed at 50% to 85%; natural gas investment at 20%.
standard_rate.source_reference: Income Tax Law (Royal Decree M/1 of 1425H), Art. 7

tax_loss_relief.description: Tax losses may be carried forward indefinitely, but the offset in any year is limited to 25% of that year's taxable profit.
tax_loss_relief.source_reference: Income Tax Law, Art. 21; Implementing Regulations

rates.description: Withholding tax on payments from Saudi residents (or PEs) to non-residents for Saudi-source income. Statutory rates; double tax treaties may reduce them.
rates.verification_note: Management fees 20%, royalties 15%, technical/consulting 5% and dividends 5% confirmed by Deloitte/ZATCA bulletin summaries. Interest 5%, rent 5%, insurance 5%, telecom 5% and 'other' 15% are the standard published table and should be confirmed against the ZATCA circular table before professional reliance.
rates.source_reference: Income Tax Law, Art. 68; Implementing Regulations, Art. 63; ZATCA Tax Bulletin Dec 2025

standard_rate.description: Standard VAT rate of 15% (increased from 5% on 1 July 2020).
standard_rate.source_reference: VAT Law (Royal Decree M/113 of 1438H); Royal Order A/638 of 2020

registration_thresholds.description: Mandatory registration above SAR 375,000 of annual taxable supplies; voluntary registration above SAR 187,500.

status.description: Saudi Arabia had not enacted a domestic minimum top-up tax as of the last review.
status.source_reference: PwC Middle East Economy Watch, Feb 2025

changelog.summary: Zakat base now applies the Article 28 maximum (equity and equivalents at year end plus the adjusted-less-book profit difference) and the full Article 27 minimum (lower of undeducted assets plus that difference, and adjusted net profit), read from ZATCA's English text of the Implementing Regulations for Zakat Collection 1445H. Two optional inputs added: year-end equity and total assets. Awaiting sign-off by the Oblique tax team.
changelog.source: ZATCA, Implementing Regulations for Zakat Collection 1445H (MR 1007 as amended by MR 1248), Articles 27 and 28

changelog.summary: First release: zakat at 2.5% of the base for a Hijri year and 2.577683% for a Gregorian year under Ministerial Resolution 1007 of 2024; income tax at 20% on the non-Saudi share; the withholding table from 5% to 20%; VAT at 15%. The Article 28 upper limit on the zakat base is not yet applied.
changelog.source: Income Tax Law (Royal Decree M/1 of 1425H); MR 1007 (2024); VAT Law
